transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, what scared me enough to come in is something happening at my job. I work in surveillance, and lately, during the quiet stretches in the monitor room, I keep hearing voices coming through the speakers. 

They say things to me, like, you missed it, Ruth, or they tell me people are going to get hurt because of me. But the thing is... every channel is completely muted. And no one else in the room hears anything at all. It just really frightened me, so I knew I needed to see someone.
Have you used any drugs or substances recently?
No, I don't use drugs. I don't really drink much either, maybe a glass of wine on a holiday, but that's about it. Nothing recently at all.
How long have you been hearing these voices?
It's been... about four months now. Yeah, right around four months. It started just after I was moved into the lead casino surveillance role.
Do you believe someone is trying to send you messages through the surveillance system?

No, I don't really think it's someone sending me a message. I mean, I know how the system works, and the channels are muted. It just... it feels like the voices are there, even though I know logically no one is broadcasting them to me. It's just happening.
Have you had any recent seizures, head injury, or other neurological illness?
No, nothing like that. I haven't had any seizures, and I haven't hit my head or anything. As far as I know, I don't have any neurological issues at all. My physical health has been fine.
Have you found yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I have. I used to look forward to a lot of different things. I'd go to salsa class, play softball, or spend time building PCs. I used to love having people over for board games, too. But lately... I don't know, I just ignore the texts when people reach out. I just sit at home, and it feels like none of it can reach me anymore.
Have you noticed yourself speaking much less than you used to?

Yeah, I have. Actually, people have started asking me to repeat myself lately because my answers just come out so slow. And it's not just talking, either. At work, I'll catch myself just staring at a report or one of the camera grids for way too long before I can even make my hands move to do anything. Everything just feels delayed.
Have you been acting in ways that other people would see as very strange or hard to make sense of?

No, not really. I mean, other than being so quiet and moving slow like I mentioned... I haven't been doing anything weird. Nobody at work or anywhere else has said I'm acting strange or doing things that don't make sense. I mostly just keep to myself, go to my shifts, and come home. So, no, I don't think so.
When you're at your slowest, do you ever become completely unable to speak or move for a period of time?

No, it's never gotten that bad. I mean, I definitely feel sluggish, and it takes me a minute to get my words out or get moving, but I've never been completely frozen or unable to speak at all. I can always force myself to do it eventually, it just... takes a lot of effort.
Do you believe that people are trying to harm you or plot against you?

No, I don't think so. I haven't noticed anyone plotting against me or trying to hurt me. I mean, my job involves watching people on the cameras and looking out for suspicious stuff, but that's just work. Outside of that, no, I don't feel like anyone is out to get me.
Have you been having these problems altogether for at least six months?
No, not quite six months. It's been... I'd say about four months now. It started right around the time I was moved into the lead casino surveillance role at work.
Since these symptoms began, have you been having a harder time keeping up with your work or daily responsibilities than you used to?

Yes, it's definitely been harder. I've already made some mistakes on my shift paperwork, which isn't like me. I've also had to step back from some activities and seeing friends because I just can't keep up the way I used to. When I'm at home, I mostly just get through the bare minimum... the basics. I'm not really cooking, hosting people, or keeping up with projects around the house anymore. It's just too much.
Since these symptoms started, have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah, I have. Most days, it's like... this heavy, gray mood just settles over me before I even manage to get out of bed. And it just kind of stays there. I'll be sitting in my car before my shift, and I can just start tearing up over nothing—literally just seeing the casino lights can make me cry. So, yes, it's pretty much all day, nearly every day.
Since these problems began, was there ever a time when the voices were happening for at least two weeks while your mood was not depressed?

No, it hasn't been like that. Before this whole stretch of feeling so hopeless and guilty—right after the surveillance lead change—I had never heard any accusations coming through the equipment. I never felt so certain I was dangerous to everyone, either. The voices and those beliefs... they really only seem to be part of this same low period. They haven't happened on their own when my mood was fine.
